deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Ramanujan derivation. It is an editorial or archival covering note, probably by G. H. Hardy, who handled Ramanujan's papers after 1920; the signature is a scrawl, so the attribution is not certain. Reading from the image, it says: 'This completes the MSS Miss S had, except for (1) what I mentioned before, (2) two short MSS about "Π_ν(x), ϖ_ρ(x)" — connected with Paper No 35. These I thought Miss S had better study a bit more.'

There is no derivation to reconstruct. The mathematical content is only a reference. Π_ν(x) and ϖ_ν(x) are the counting functions for integers ≤ x with exactly ν prime factors: one counts distinct prime factors (or squarefree numbers), the other counts prime factors with multiplicity. These are the functions used by Hardy and Ramanujan in their work on the normal number of prime factors.

'Paper No 35' is most plausibly the numbering in Ramanujan's Collected Papers (1927). There No. 35 is, I believe, Hardy & Ramanujan, 'The normal number of prime factors of a number n' (Quart. J. Math. 48 (1917)). That paper studies π_ν(x) and ϖ_ν(x) and proves bounds of the type π_ν(x) < C x (log log x + c)^{ν-1} / ((ν-1)! log x). This identification is my inference, not stated on the page.

So the note says that two short unpublished Ramanujan manuscripts on these functions were held back for further study by 'Miss S'. Her identity is unsure; she may have been a copyist or transcriber working on the Ramanujan papers. The previous page is a fair copy of Ramanujan's speculative claims about 'Mersenne's primes'. The next page begins a list of queries ('(3) Is there not a confusion ... on p 3'), so this folio belongs to editorial correspondence about the manuscripts.

results.what: Reference to two short unpublished manuscripts on the prime-factor counting functions Π_ν(x), ϖ_ρ(x), linked to 'Paper No 35' (presumably Hardy–Ramanujan, normal number of prime factors, 1917)
results.modern_name: Counting functions for integers with k prime factors (Landau's π_k(x) ~ x (log log x)^{k-1}/((k-1)! log x)); Hardy–Ramanujan normal order of ω(n)
results.usually_credited_to: Landau (1900, 1909) for the asymptotic of π_k(x); Hardy & Ramanujan (1917) for the uniform bounds and normal order

transcription_corrections: The page is in a different hand from Ramanujan's, probably Hardy's; the signature is a scrawl and reading it as 'GHH' is uncertain.
The shelfmark at the top reads 'Add Ms a 94 18(11)', with folio number (11) circled.
The second symbol reads ϖ with subscript ρ, i.e. '\varpi_\rho(x)'. The subscript could equally be ν in a hasty hand; ν would match Π_ν(x) and the paper's notation.
